hero.headline: Trump names housing official Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, a housing official, to serve as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard in the role. Multiple news organizations including CNBC, CNN, NBC News, Axios, and Bloomberg confirmed the appointment.

The director of national intelligence oversees 18 intelligence agencies including the CIA, NSA, and FBI. This position was established after the September 11 attacks to coordinate intelligence gathering and sharing across federal agencies. The director serves as the principal intelligence advisor to the president and the National Security Council.

Pulte's appointment marks another shift in Trump's national security team. Gabbard, a former Democratic congresswoman from Hawaii who later joined the Republican Party, had been serving in the intelligence leadership role. The reasons for her departure were not specified in available reports.

The acting designation allows Pulte to serve in the position temporarily without requiring Senate confirmation. Permanent directors of national intelligence must be approved by the Senate. Trump has frequently used acting appointments to staff key positions, a strategy that enables faster personnel changes but can raise questions about long-term leadership stability in sensitive national security roles.

According to the reports, Pulte has been characterized as a top housing official and regulatory figure. His background in housing administration represents a different career path than is typical for intelligence leadership roles. Some outlets described him as a "controversial" pick for the position, suggesting his appointment may draw scrutiny from lawmakers and analysts.

The transition in the intelligence directorship comes as Trump continues reorganizing his administration following his election. The use of acting appointments has been a consistent feature of his staffing approach, allowing him to place individuals in leadership positions quickly while avoiding the Senate confirmation process that can be time-consuming and contentious.

Gabbard's departure from the intelligence directorship follows her previous role as director of the Defense Intelligence Agency during Trump's first term. Her transition to a different position or her reasons for leaving the intelligence directorship have not been detailed in the available reports.

The appointment of Pulte to oversee the nation's intelligence agencies represents a significant personnel change in an area of government with substantial national security implications. As the intelligence community continues to address evolving threats and challenges, questions may arise about the experience and background of leadership overseeing 18 separate intelligence agencies and coordinating their operations across the government.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran negotiations continue despite reports of suspension
cards.teaser: The president defended ongoing diplomatic efforts with Iran as multiple news outlets reported conflicting accounts of the status of talks.
cards.body:
President Trump says negotiations with Iran continue, dismissing reports that talks have been suspended. He emphasized that reaching an agreement is a complex undertaking.

The diplomatic efforts have been complicated by the situation in Lebanon, where clashes between Israel and Hezbollah persist despite both sides accepting a US-proposed partial ceasefire plan. A cessation of hostilities in Lebanon is viewed as essential to advancing talks between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Rubio testifies before Senate as Iran ceasefire negotiations stall
cards.teaser: The secretary of state appeared before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee to discuss the State Department budget request.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Tuesday regarding the State Department's budget request. The hearing occurred as diplomatic efforts to end the three-month war with Iran encountered difficulties, despite recent optimism from President Trump about reaching a deal to halt hostilities and remove sanctions.

The testimony addressed the direction of ongoing negotiations with Tehran. On the same day, Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche also appeared before the House.

cards.headline: Trump Proposes 25% Tariff on Brazilian Imports
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced a proposal to impose a 25% tariff on imports from Brazil, citing what it describes as unfair trade practices. The tariff plan represents the administration's latest attempt to advance its trade agenda through Section 301 investigations, a mechanism that allows the U.S. government to investigate and respond to foreign trade practices it considers harmful to American interests.

Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 gives the U.S. Trade Representative authority to investigate complaints about foreign trade barriers and unfair practices. The administration has increasingly relied on these investigations to justify tariffs and other trade measures. The proposed 25% rate would apply broadly to Brazilian goods entering the United States.

Brazil ranks as a major U.S. trading partner, with significant exports including agricultural products, steel, and manufactured goods. A 25% tariff would substantially increase costs for American companies that import Brazilian materials and products, potentially affecting supply chains across multiple industries. The measure could also strain diplomatic relations between the two largest economies in the Americas.

The proposal comes as the administration works to rebuild its tariff framework after earlier trade measures faced legal challenges and diplomatic pushback. Previous tariff programs under Section 301 have targeted China and other countries, with mixed economic results. Critics of broad tariff policies argue they raise costs for American businesses and consumers, while supporters contend they protect domestic industries and provide leverage in trade negotiations.

This proposed tariff reflects a broader pattern of trade measures that have already shaped business operations across the country. Hundreds of thousands of importers paid substantial tariff fees under previous Trump administration policies, leading to significant refund claims once the Supreme Court struck down those measures. The refund process that followed demonstrated how tariff policies can create complex cascading effects throughout supply chains and business operations.

The tariff proposal will likely face a review period during which businesses and other stakeholders can submit comments. Brazil's government has not yet publicly responded to the announcement. The final implementation timeline and any potential exemptions remain to be determined as the investigation proceeds.

For American companies relying on Brazilian imports, the proposed 25% tariff represents a significant concern. Businesses that previously paid tariffs under other administration policies understand the potential financial impact of such measures. The refund processes that followed earlier tariffs illustrated both the complexities involved and the substantial amounts of money at stake for importers.

The administration's continued reliance on Section 301 investigations signals that tariff-based trade policy will remain a central component of its economic strategy. Whether this approach successfully addresses the administration's trade concerns or creates additional economic friction remains uncertain as the investigation into Brazilian trade practices proceeds.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes Kill 18 in Ukraine After Week of Threats
cards.body:
Russian forces launched a massive bombardment against Ukraine, killing at least 18 people and injuring dozens more across multiple cities. The assault involved 73 missiles and 656 drones, including eight hypersonic Tsirkon missiles, according to Ukraine's air force. The primary targets were Kyiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Poltava, and Kharkiv.

The attack came after Russia spent a week issuing repeated warnings of a major offensive. This delay between threats and actual strikes appeared designed to impose psychological pressure on Ukrainian civilians. Residents sheltered in basements, corridors, and metro stations as loud explosions rocked cities and black smoke filled the air.

In Kyiv, six people died and 66 were injured, including three children. A missile struck a 24-story apartment building, causing it to collapse. Other buildings caught fire, including a nine-story block. In one district, cars burned from falling missile debris, and fires broke out near a kindergarten. Power was cut for 140,000 residents, though utility workers later restored electricity to 110,000 people.

The destruction was particularly severe in Dnipro, where at least 12 people were killed and 37 injured. A four-story residential building collapsed, burying a three-year-old boy. Six people remained missing under the rubble, and a rescue worker was killed in a secondary strike. The city's mayor accused Russia of deliberately using cluster munitions in populated areas to maximize civilian casualties, posting images of shattered roads and damaged homes.

Ukraine's air defenses intercepted roughly half of the incoming missiles, but more than 30 struck civilian targets. Kharkiv saw at least 14 injured, with residential homes and vehicles damaged across the city.

The bombardment prompted President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to appeal directly to Donald Trump for Patriot missile systems. Zelenskyy emphasized that Ukraine is running out of Patriot interceptors, which are the only air defense systems capable of stopping fast-moving ballistic missiles. He described Patriots as a "vital tool" for saving lives and noted that ballistic missiles represent Moscow's "last major advantage on the battlefield." The Trump administration has not yet responded to these requests.

Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, characterized the strikes as evidence that Russia is losing. He stated that Moscow has no remaining options except terror and that battlefield losses mean no amount of missiles can change the outcome. He called Putin "a war criminal and loser."

The attacks underscore the intensity of the conflict as both sides face mounting pressure. Ukraine has recently waged an increasingly successful aerial campaign with long-range drones, striking Russian oil refineries, ports, and supply corridors. The Russian strikes appear aimed at strengthening Moscow's negotiating position as international pressure builds for talks to end the war.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Backing Down From Beirut Threat
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Netanyahu held off attacking Beirut under pressure from President Trump but vowed to continue fighting Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel launched strikes on southern Lebanon after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu withdrew threats to attack Beirut. Under pressure from President Trump, Netanyahu stepped back from the Beirut operation but pledged to continue military operations against Hezbollah.

The fighting continues despite Israel and Hezbollah accepting a US-proposed partial ceasefire plan. A halt to hostilities between the two groups is seen as essential to broader peace efforts with Iran, which backs Hezbollah. The White House is pushing for a deal, though Iran has signaled it wants concessions before agreeing to de-escalation.

cards.headline: Trump adjusts tariffs on steel, aluminum, and copper imports
cards.teaser: The president lowered tariffs on some aluminum and steel derivative products, including agricultural equipment and HVAC systems.
cards.body:
President Trump adjusted tariffs on certain aluminum, copper, and steel imports. A proclamation lowered tariffs on some aluminum and steel derivative products from 25 percent to 15 percent, including agricultural equipment and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems.

Trump had initially imposed 25 percent tariffs on aluminum and steel. The adjustment affects specific product categories while maintaining the broader tariff structure on base metals.

cards.headline: Russia Faces Setbacks in Ukraine as War Strategy Questioned
cards.teaser: Moscow has failed to achieve its war aims in Ukraine, prompting debate over how President Putin can exit the conflict.
cards.body:
Russia has not achieved its objectives in Ukraine, creating pressure on President Putin to find a way out of the conflict. The setbacks have fueled discontent inside Russia and raised doubts about Moscow's strategy. Observers suggest Putin could face personal consequences for the failures.

Ukraine recently changed its tactics on the battlefield, contributing to Russian losses. The shift has put Putin in a position where he slowly appears to be losing ground. Mounting casualties and battlefield defeats have left the Kremlin without a clear path forward in the war.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Backing Down From Beirut Threat
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Netanyahu held off attacking Beirut under pressure from President Trump but vowed to continue fighting Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel launched strikes on southern Lebanon after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu withdrew threats to attack Beirut. Under pressure from President Trump, Netanyahu stepped back from the Beirut operation but pledged to continue military operations against Hezbollah.

The fighting continues despite Israel and Hezbollah accepting a US-proposed partial ceasefire plan. A halt to hostilities between the two groups is seen as essential to broader peace efforts with Iran, which backs Hezbollah. The White House is pushing for a deal, though Iran has signaled it wants concessions before agreeing to de-escalation.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Drone Tactics Force Shift in Israeli Strategy in Lebanon
cards.teaser: Israel's Lebanon campaign has stalled as Hezbollah demonstrates greater capability than at the start of the conflict.
cards.body:
An Israeli military campaign that began with high expectations has reached an impasse in Lebanon. Hezbollah's use of drones has fundamentally altered the conflict's trajectory, forcing Israel to adjust its strategy. The Lebanese group appears more capable now than when fighting began.

A ceasefire plan backed by the US has been accepted by both Israel and Hezbollah, though clashes continue. The cessation of hostilities is viewed as crucial to broader peace efforts involving Iran, which has suspended talks with the U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Says Country Failing Jewish Canadians
cards.teaser: Mark Carney acknowledged a crisis of antisemitism after Jewish organizations called for government action.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is failing its Jewish citizens, describing a crisis of antisemitism in the country. His comments came in response to calls from Jewish organizations for the government to address what they characterized as a growing problem. Carney acknowledged the severity of the situation.

Jewish groups had pressed the government to take action against rising antisemitism. The organizations described the situation as a crisis requiring immediate attention. Carney's public acknowledgment represents a shift in how the government is addressing concerns from the Jewish community.

cards.headline: Ghana President to Review Anti-LGBTQ Bill Before Approval
cards.teaser: The bill, passed by parliament, proposes prison sentences for people identifying as LGBTQ.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament approved a sweeping bill that criminalizes LGBTQ+ activity and identifying as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, or queer. The legislation mandates prison sentences of three to 10 years for those affected. President John Dramani Mahama said the bill will be scrutinized before final approval.

LGBTQ+ community groups have expressed serious concerns about the law's impact. Rights advocates warn that people fear losing their homes, jobs, and access to healthcare if the legislation is ratified. The bill's passage has drawn international attention for its harsh penalties targeting sexual and gender minorities.

cards.headline: Hackers Trick Instagram AI Chatbot to Access User Accounts
cards.teaser: Security breach reportedly linked to recent hijackings of high-profile Instagram accounts.
cards.body:
Hackers exploited Instagram's AI chatbot to gain unauthorized access to user accounts. The manipulation of the automated system created a security vulnerability that bypassed normal protective measures.

The incident has been linked to recent cases involving compromised high-profile Instagram accounts, raising concerns about the reliability of AI-powered tools in customer service systems on social media platforms.

A cessation of hostilities in Lebanon is viewed as essential to advancing talks between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 18 people including child
cards.teaser: Rescue workers pulled bodies from rubble after attacks on residential areas left nearly two dozen dead.
cards.body:
Russian military strikes on Ukraine killed 18 people, including an eight-year-old boy and a woman who died when an apartment block was hit. The attacks targeted residential areas across multiple Ukrainian cities.

Rescue teams worked through the rubble to recover victims from the damaged buildings. Some people remained trapped under the debris following the overnight strikes.

cards.headline: Trump administration addresses congressional concerns over Justice Department settlement fund
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers sought assurances about the future of a $1.8 billion fund as administration officials worked to advance legislative priorities.
cards.body:
Trump administration officials met with congressional Republicans to discuss a Justice Department settlement fund that has become a point of contention. Republican senators have sought clear commitments about the fund's future as the administration pursues its legislative priorities.

The Justice Department says it "disagrees strongly" with a court ruling that halted the $1.8 billion fund, which the administration characterizes as an "anti-weaponisation" initiative. The Trump administration indicated it would abide by the court's decision while the matter remains under review.

cards.headline: Hackers exploit Instagram AI chatbot to access user accounts
cards.teaser: Security researchers found that attackers tricked the platform's artificial intelligence tool into providing unauthorized account access.
cards.body:
Hackers have tricked Instagram's AI chatbot into providing access to other users' accounts. The incident has been linked to recent hijackings of high-profile Instagram accounts.

The breach highlights security concerns around AI-powered customer service tools deployed by major social media platforms.

cards.headline: UK Athletics fined after Paralympian dies in training ground accident
cards.teaser: A judge ordered the organization to pay 350,000 pounds plus costs following the death of an athlete struck by falling equipment.
cards.body:
A judge at the Old Bailey fined UK Athletics £350,000 with £44,000 in costs following the death of Paralympic athlete Abdullah Hayayei. The 36-year-old UAE athlete was killed in July 2017 when a 440lb practice throwing cage fell on him at Newham Leisure Centre in east London.

Hayayei was preparing to compete at the World Para Athletics Championships when the accident occurred. The court ruled the death was "wholly avoidable," highlighting failings in safety procedures at the training facility.

cards.headline: Former SNP chief executive admits to embezzling 400,000 pounds from party
cards.teaser: Peter Murrell faces a lengthy prison sentence after pleading guilty to using party credit cards for personal spending.
cards.body:
Peter Murrell, the former chief executive of the Scottish National Party, has admitted to embezzling £400,000 from the party. He used SNP credit cards to fund a spending spree on personal expenses.

Following his guilty plea, Murrell faces a lengthy jail sentence for the theft. The case represents one of the largest financial scandals to affect a major British political party in recent years.

cards.headline: Marvell Stock Jumps 20% After Nvidia CEO Endorsement
cards.teaser: Shares of chip designer Marvell surged after Nvidia's CEO suggested the company could reach a trillion-dollar valuation.
cards.body:
Marvell Technology's stock surged 20% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang suggested the company could become the next trillion-dollar company. The endorsement coincided with Marvell's announcement of a new 102.4 Tbps switch built for AI and cloud data center infrastructure.

Marvell specializes in chips and switches for data centers, capitalizing on growing demand from artificial intelligence applications. Huang's public backing from the world's dominant AI chip manufacturer provided significant validation for the company's position in the high-growth AI infrastructure market.

cards.headline: Anthropic Files for Public Offering
cards.teaser: The AI company backed by major tech investors has filed paperwork for an initial public offering that could value it in the trillions.
cards.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, has filed confidentially for an initial public offering on the US stock market. The filing comes after the company raised $65 billion in funding, valuing it at $965 billion. This represents significant growth from its $380 billion valuation in February.

The IPO filing positions Anthropic among major technology firms expected to go public this year, including SpaceX and OpenAI. The company has attracted enterprise customers and established itself as a competitor in the large language model space.

cards.headline: Short-Seller Andrew Left Convicted of Securities Fraud
cards.teaser: A federal jury found the prominent investor guilty of fraud, raising concerns among others who bet against companies.
cards.body:
Andrew Left, an investor who gained attention for betting against company stocks, was convicted of securities fraud by a federal jury. Left became well-known in financial circles for his short-selling activities, which involve borrowing shares to sell them in anticipation of price declines. The conviction marks a significant legal development for an investor who built a public profile around his market positions.

The case has prompted concern among other short-sellers about potential implications for their activities. Short-selling plays a role in financial markets by providing price discovery and liquidity, though it remains controversial when practitioners publicly criticize companies they are betting against.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Reports Sales Growth Driven by Bras
cards.teaser: The retailer exceeded earnings expectations and raised its annual guidance as its brand momentum continues.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret reported first-quarter earnings that beat analyst estimates, with the company attributing the performance to strong sales of bras and other core products. The retailer raised its full-year financial guidance following the results. The quarter showed continued momentum for a brand that has worked to reposition itself in the lingerie market.

Bra sales specifically drove the turnaround, indicating customer response to the company's product offerings. Victoria's Secret has focused on its foundational categories as part of a broader strategy to rebuild market position after years of declining sales and brand challenges.

cards.headline: Martin Scorsese Backs AI Image Generation Startup
cards.teaser: The filmmaker's investment in Black Forest Labs signals Hollywood's changing stance on artificial intelligence technology.
cards.body:
Director Martin Scorsese has invested in Black Forest Labs, a startup developing AI-powered image generation technology. The investment signals a shift in Hollywood's perspective on artificial intelligence, a technology that has sparked substantial debate within the entertainment industry.

The backing from such a prominent filmmaker represents a high-profile endorsement of AI tools in creative production. It reflects what appears to be a softening stance on artificial intelligence across Hollywood, even as the industry continues to grapple with questions about AI's role in production and its broader implications.

cards.headline: Instagram AI Chatbot Exploited in Account Breach
cards.teaser: Hackers manipulated the platform's AI assistant to gain unauthorized access to user accounts.
cards.body:
Hackers discovered a way to manipulate Instagram's AI chatbot into granting unauthorized access to user accounts. By exploiting how the system responds to certain requests, attackers were able to bypass standard security protections.

The incident connects to recent high-profile Instagram account hijackings. The discovery underscores the security risks that emerge as social media platforms deploy AI assistants alongside their core services.

hero.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch AI-powered Windows PCs
hero.body:
Nvidia and Microsoft have unveiled a new generation of Windows personal computers built around artificial intelligence capabilities. The partnership marks what Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang calls a reinvention of the PC for the age of personal AI, arriving after three years of collaboration between the two companies.

The centerpiece of the announcement is Nvidia's RTX Spark chip, a superchip combining a microprocessor and graphics processor. Developed with assistance from Taiwan's MediaTek, the chip is designed to run AI agents locally on devices rather than relying on cloud computing. This approach would allow AI agents to navigate computers autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions as the primary way users control their machines.

Huang described the development as reinventing the PC for the first time in 40 years. The chip will power computers from major manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus, and HP, all running Microsoft Windows. Despite the powerful capabilities, Nvidia says computers using the chip will remain thin and light.

The move represents a significant expansion for Nvidia beyond its dominant position in data center AI semiconductors. The company is also developing the Vera CPU, designed for AI agents and already being adopted by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX. Together, these products demonstrate Nvidia's growing focus on PC and CPU products alongside its existing graphics card business.

Industry analysts view the launch as strategically important but potentially a longer-term opportunity. Neil Shah, co-founder of Counterpoint Research, compared the RTX Spark moment to major technological shifts like the iPhone and ChatGPT, predicting that agentic AI personal computers will become commonplace in homes within coming years. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, noted that while the move reinforces Huang's vision of PCs evolving into hyperintelligent digital co-workers, investors likely view it as a longer-term growth opportunity rather than an immediate earnings driver.

The announcement has intensified competition in consumer AI chips. Intel plans to ship its own AI chip later this year with cheaper memory and cooling technology, introducing a graphics processing unit codenamed Crescent Island. The company also faces competition from Apple and Qualcomm.

When asked about concerns that AI might eliminate software engineering jobs, Huang dismissed the notion. "This is complete nonsense," he said, arguing that AI increases worker productivity and leads to more software engineers being hired rather than fewer.

The launch comes as major technology companies race to integrate AI into consumer products. The success of Nvidia and Microsoft's platform will depend on whether consumers and businesses find genuine value in running AI applications locally on their machines compared to existing cloud-based alternatives.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemini Spark, AI assistant that runs continuously
cards.teaser: The new AI agent can automate tasks and access user information around the clock.
cards.body:
Google has launched Gemini Spark, a new AI agent designed to work autonomously on behalf of users. The assistant can access personal information and complete tasks without being directly prompted, positioning it as a competitor to similar agentic AI products from other companies.

Reviewers who tested Gemini Spark found it capable of handling complex requests like trip planning, though they noted significant privacy concerns. The level of access required raises questions about the tradeoffs between convenience and data security, with some describing the experience as both impressive and unsettling.

cards.headline: Blue Origin plans second New Glenn launch after rocket explosion
cards.teaser: The company says launchpad damage was less severe than expected following last week's incident.
cards.body:
Blue Origin plans to launch its New Glenn rocket again this year following an explosion at its Florida launchpad. CEO Dave Limp said the damage to the facility was less severe than initially expected, enabling the company to move forward with repair and preparation efforts.

The explosion occurred during a test at Cape Canaveral. Blue Origin has not revealed what caused the incident.

cards.headline: Impulse Space raises $500 million for orbital maneuvering technology
cards.teaser: The rocket engine startup plans to use the funding to hire engineers rather than invest in automation.
cards.body:
Impulse Space, a rocket engine startup, secured $500 million in funding to expand its workforce. President Eric Romo emphasized that the company will prioritize hiring human engineers, stating that designing physical systems requires human expertise that AI cannot yet replace.

The funding underscores growing investor confidence in the orbital maneuvering sector as demand for in-orbit mobility solutions increases. Romo expects the market will continue to discover new applications for the technology as more satellites and spacecraft require repositioning capabilities.

cards.headline: Energy Department restarts rebate program with new restrictions
cards.teaser: Homeowners can no longer get rebates for switching from fossil fuels to electric heating.
cards.body:
The Department of Energy restarted its energy rebate program with modified eligibility rules. Households switching from fossil fuel heating systems to electric heat pumps are no longer covered under the program. The change represents a shift in the program's approach to home energy efficiency.

The rebate program previously encouraged homeowners to electrify heating systems as part of broader climate goals. The new restrictions limit what types of energy upgrades qualify for federal rebates, though the program continues to cover other household efficiency improvements.

cards.headline: Pacific Fusion prototype generates 440 gigawatts in brief pulse
cards.teaser: The fusion energy company's scaled-down test delivered enormous power in an 80-nanosecond burst.
cards.body:
Pacific Fusion's latest prototype successfully generated 440 gigawatts of power during an 80-nanosecond pulse. This sub-scale test demonstrates the company's progress toward building a demonstration power plant.

The company is advancing its design approach for a larger demonstration facility based on these results. Pacific Fusion's technical method relies on delivering massive amounts of power in brief bursts rather than sustained continuous output.

cards.headline: NASA rover captures high-resolution Mars panorama
cards.teaser: Clear atmospheric conditions allowed one of the sharpest wide-angle images of the planet's surface.
cards.body:

hero.headline: Sir Kenny Dalglish undergoing cancer treatment
hero.body:
Sir Kenny Dalglish, the legendary Scottish footballer and manager, has confirmed he is receiving treatment for cancer. The 75-year-old made the announcement on Tuesday after accidentally posting about his treatment on social media earlier that day.

Dalglish revealed the news in a statement addressing the inadvertent disclosure. He said: "As my inadvertent social media post has indicated, I am currently undergoing treatment for cancer. Unlike my mobile phone use, the treatment is going well."

The Liverpool icon expressed his preference that the matter had remained private. He continued: "Ideally, this would have remained private because that's the way it should be, but my useless technology skills have forced my hand. Obviously I did not mean to make this matter public so I would appreciate it if the privacy of my family and myself are respected."

Dalglish took the opportunity to praise the medical staff involved in his care. He stated: "As ever, thank you to the wonderful medical staff who have shown incredible care and discretion, not just for me but for many, many others. They are a credit to themselves."

Liverpool Football Club issued a statement expressing their support, saying: "The support, best wishes and love of everyone at Liverpool FC are, and will be, with Sir Kenny and his family." The club also joined Dalglish in requesting privacy during this time.

The announcement has resonated throughout the football world, with the Scottish great receiving widespread messages of support from across the sport. Dalglish's connection to Liverpool remains deep, having been integral to the club's success both during his playing days and managerial tenure.

Beginning his career with Celtic before joining Liverpool, Dalglish became one of football's most celebrated figures. He achieved significant success at club level and earned more than 100 caps for Scotland, scoring 30 international goals. His managerial experience extended beyond Liverpool to include spells with Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United.

Beyond his achievements on the pitch, Dalglish is widely respected for his role in supporting Liverpool and the broader football community following the Hillsborough disaster in 1989. His dignified leadership during that tragedy has cemented his status as a figure of considerable moral authority within the sport.

At 75 years old, Dalglish has remained a visible presence in football, regularly attending Liverpool matches and participating in club events. His decision to eventually reveal his cancer diagnosis, despite his initial preference for privacy, reflects the circumstances of the accidental social media post rather than any planned public announcement.

cards.headline: UK Athletics fined £350,000 over Paralympian's death
cards.teaser: A judge has fined UK Athletics £350,000 after a Paralympic athlete died when equipment fell on him at a training ground in east London.
cards.body:
UK Athletics has been fined £350,000 with £44,000 in costs following the death of Paralympian Abdullah Hayayei. The 36-year-old UAE athlete died in July 2017 when a 440lb practice throwing cage fell on him at Newham Leisure Centre in east London.

Hayayei, a father of five, was preparing for the World Para Athletics Championships when the fatal accident occurred. A judge at the Old Bailey described the death as "wholly avoidable," highlighting serious safety failures by the organisation that resulted in the tragic incident.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots for two draft picks
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia Eagles have agreed to trade wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots in exchange for two draft picks.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots on Monday, ending months of speculation about the star receiver's future. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, will reunite with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. The Eagles receive a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 in the deal.

Brown had grown frustrated during his time in Philadelphia. The trade significantly reshapes the Eagles' offense while providing the Patriots with a major addition to their receiving corps.

cards.headline: Liverpool in advanced talks to hire Andoni Iraola
cards.teaser: Liverpool are in advanced negotiations with Andoni Iraola to become their next head coach after the dismissal of Arne Slot.
cards.body:
Liverpool have opened formal talks with Andoni Iraola to become their new head coach, following Arne Slot's sacking on Saturday. The Spanish manager is the clear frontrunner for the Anfield position.

Iraola's aggressive, front-footed style of play aligns with Liverpool's tactical preferences, an approach the club felt was missing during Slot's second season in charge. Liverpool are aiming to complete the appointment before the World Cup begins.

cards.headline: Milan Momcilovic commits to Kentucky, reportedly for $6 million
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State star Milan Momcilovic has committed to Kentucky in the college basketball transfer portal, reportedly receiving a substantial financial package.
cards.body:
Momcilovic, ranked as the top transfer available in the portal, chose Kentucky over Arizona and other suitors. The commitment gives head coach Mark Pope a significant addition to his roster for the upcoming season.

Reports indicate Momcilovic's deal is worth approximately $6 million, reflecting the new financial landscape of college athletics. The forward's decision represents one of the highest-profile transfers in this cycle.

cards.headline: Stanley Cup Final begins with Hurricanes facing Golden Knights
cards.teaser: The Carolina Hurricanes and Vegas Golden Knights are set to face off in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Both teams are preparing for the championship series, with analysts breaking down the top players and key matchups. The Hurricanes' defense is viewed as a potential factor that could limit Vegas' offensive production in the opening game.

Ticket prices for the Final have drawn attention, with fans expressing shock at the cost of resale seats. Both Ticketmaster and the Hurricanes have responded to concerns about the steep prices for attending games in the series.

cards.headline: Switzerland travel to World Cup without Breel Embolo
cards.teaser: Switzerland's World Cup squad has traveled to the United States without forward Breel Embolo after his Esta authorization was placed under review.
cards.body:
Switzerland's World Cup squad has travelled to the United States without forward Breel Embolo. The player's Esta authorisation, which is required for entry into the country, is currently under review by authorities.

The absence of one of Switzerland's key attacking players means the team will need to adjust their squad selection and tactics as they prepare for the tournament.

hero.headline: Welsh Actor Owain Rhys Davies Dies at 44
hero.body:
Owain Rhys Davies, a Welsh actor known for his role in Twin Peaks: The Return, died over the weekend, according to the BBC. He was 44. His brother said Davies died suddenly, naturally, and peacefully. The family described the death as sudden and said questions remain unanswered about the circumstances.

Davies appeared as FBI Agent Wilson in the 2017 revival of David Lynch's Twin Peaks, performing in three episodes alongside Lynch himself. The revival brought back the cult classic series nearly three decades after its original run. Davies also had a role in the Netflix science fiction series The OA, which ran from 2016 to 2019.

Born in Wales, Davies built his career across British and American television productions. His work in Twin Peaks: The Return placed him in one of the most anticipated television events of 2017, when the show returned after 25 years off the air. The series was a critical success and introduced the original show to a new generation of viewers.

Davies' family has not released additional information about the cause of death. His sudden passing has prompted tributes from colleagues in the entertainment industry. The actor's work in both British and American productions gave him recognition on both sides of the Atlantic.

Davies leaves behind a body of work that includes appearances in two notable series that garnered devoted followings. His role in Twin Peaks: The Return connected him to one of television's most influential creators and a franchise that has maintained cultural relevance for more than three decades.

cards.headline: BTS to Headline iHeartRadio Festival in Las Vegas
cards.teaser: The K-pop group will perform at the two-day September event alongside Cardi B, Lainey Wilson, and other artists.
cards.body:
BTS will headline the iHeartRadio Festival in Las Vegas in September, marking another major performance in the city for the K-pop group. The announcement came Tuesday from iHeartRadio, which hosts the annual two-day music event.

Cardi B, Lainey Wilson, Benson Boone, and Zara Larsson are also set to perform at the festival. BTS has previously performed in Las Vegas, establishing the city as a regular stop for the group's major appearances. The festival typically draws large crowds and features artists across multiple genres.

cards.headline: Netflix Launches Book Adaptation Hub for Readers
cards.teaser: The streaming service created a dedicated page featuring series like Bridgerton and other book-to-screen adaptations.
cards.body:
Netflix launched a new hub Tuesday focused on book adaptations, bringing together series and films based on literature in one location. The page, called Watch Your Favorite Books, includes Bridgerton, The Gray Man, and other titles adapted from written works.

The streamer described the hub as targeting nine different reader types and converting reading lists into viewing queues. The initiative reflects Netflix's ongoing investment in literary adaptations, which have become a significant part of its content strategy. The hub aims to help subscribers discover content based on books they may have read or want to read.

cards.headline: Idris Elba and Ice Skating Champions Receive Royal Honours
cards.teaser: King Charles presented honours at Windsor Castle to the actor and the skating duo Torvill and Dean.
cards.body:
Actor Idris Elba and ice skating champions Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean received honours from King Charles at Windsor Castle on Tuesday. Actress and comedian Meera Syal was also among those recognized during the ceremony.

The investiture ceremony is part of the regular honours system in which the monarch recognizes individuals for their contributions to British culture and society.

cards.headline: Masters of the Universe Film Opens Nearly 40 Years After Original
cards.teaser: The new adaptation features Nicholas Galitzine as He-Man in a return to the Mattel franchise.
cards.body:
A new Masters of the Universe film has been released, nearly four decades after the 1987 Cannon Films version that performed poorly at the box office. Nicholas Galitzine stars as He-Man in the sci-fi fantasy adventure based on the Mattel toy line and media franchise.

Reviews describe the film as delightfully silly and a perfect sci-fi fantasy adventure. The original franchise was popular in the 1980s before declining in cultural prominence. The new film attempts to revive interest in the He-Man character and the broader Masters of the Universe mythology for contemporary audiences.

cards.headline: Ranveer Singh Exit From Don 3 Sparks Bollywood Dispute
cards.teaser: The actor's departure in December triggered a standoff involving 25 senior film industry figures and an audit.
cards.body:
Actor Ranveer Singh's exit from Don 3 in December 2025 has led to a major dispute in Bollywood involving approximately 25 senior industry figures. The conflict has resulted in a Big Four audit and has gone through the Producers Guild of India.

The standoff represents one of the most significant industry disputes in Bollywood in recent years. Singh is one of the top actors in the Indian film industry, and his departure from the franchise film created ripples throughout the production community. The Don franchise has been a significant property in Bollywood cinema.

cards.headline: Mindy Kaling Debuts First Solo-Created Show Since The Mindy Project
cards.teaser: Hulu's Not Suitable for Work marks Kaling's first series with sole creator credit in years, exploring workplace life.
cards.body:
Mindy Kaling's new Hulu series Not Suitable for Work has arrived, representing her first show with sole creator credit since The Mindy Project. The sitcom follows five friends navigating life and love across two Manhattan apartments, with a more diverse cast than the shows that inspired it.

The series continues Kaling's pattern of exploring different life stages through television. After creating Netflix's Never Have I Ever set in high school and HBO Max's The Sex Lives of College Girls focused on college life, Not Suitable for Work moves into the professional world and early adulthood.

hero.headline: Trump adjusts tariffs on steel, aluminum, and copper imports
hero.teaser: The president lowered tariffs on some aluminum and steel derivative products, including agricultural equipment and HVAC systems.
hero.body:
President Trump adjusted tariffs on certain aluminum, copper, and steel imports. A proclamation lowered tariffs on some aluminum and steel derivative products from 25 percent to 15 percent, including agricultural equipment and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems.

Trump had initially imposed 25 percent tariffs on aluminum and steel. The adjustment affects specific product categories while maintaining the broader tariff structure on base metals.

cards.headline: Bolton says Iran expects Trump to make concessions in ceasefire talks
cards.teaser: The former national security adviser said Iran is using oil price fluctuations as leverage in negotiations with the United States.
cards.body:
Former national security adviser John Bolton said Iran is using oil price fluctuations as leverage in ceasefire talks with the United States. Bolton believes Iran calculates that domestic political pressure will force President Trump toward making concessions, betting that the U.S. administration is eager to reach a deal.

The assessment reflects broader negotiations aimed at ending hostilities between the two countries. The White House is pushing for an agreement amid polling pressure and demands from Gulf allies, while Iran continues to demand concessions as a condition for advancing talks.

cards.headline: Rubio testifies before Senate as Iran ceasefire negotiations stall
cards.teaser: The secretary of state appeared before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee to discuss the State Department budget request.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Tuesday regarding the State Department's budget request. The hearing occurred as diplomatic efforts to end the three-month war with Iran encountered difficulties, despite recent optimism from President Trump about reaching a deal to halt hostilities and remove sanctions.

The testimony addressed the direction of ongoing negotiations with Tehran. On the same day, Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche also appeared before the House.

cards.headline: O'Reilly predicts Newark ICE protests will not affect DHS policy
cards.teaser: The political commentator said protests at an immigration detention facility in Newark are better organized than those in Minneapolis.
cards.body:
Political commentator Bill O'Reilly said Monday that protests at an immigration detention facility in Newark, New Jersey, will likely have no effect on Department of Homeland Security policy.

O'Reilly made the comments while discussing the ongoing demonstrations at the facility.

cards.headline: Democratic strategist to discuss Platner controversies and Biden memoir backlash
cards.teaser: The Hill will host a discussion on the Maine Senate candidate and the former first lady's upcoming book.
cards.body:
The Hill scheduled a discussion on the growing controversy surrounding Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner and backlash to former first lady Jill Biden's upcoming memoir. Democratic strategist Steve Schale will join the conversation titled The Fight for 2028.

The discussion will also cover competition between Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Hosts Amie Parnes and Ian Swanson will lead the panel.

cards.headline: Opinion: Remote work has become critical economic infrastructure
cards.teaser: A columnist argues Congress should pay attention to the economic role of remote work arrangements.
cards.body:
A columnist argued that remote work has become critical economic infrastructure despite congressional focus on productivity and deficits. The piece suggests Congress is overlooking the economic significance of remote work policies.

The opinion piece frames remote work as having evolved beyond a temporary arrangement into a fundamental part of the economy. The author urges lawmakers to recognize this shift in their policy considerations.

cards.headline: Opinion: Florida voter examines gerrymandering and political strategy
cards.teaser: A columnist discusses how a politician used redistricting challenges to advance her position.
cards.body:
A columnist wrote that a Florida politician used a Republican effort targeting Black voting power to secure a safer seat for herself. The piece examines the intersection of gerrymandering and individual political strategy.

The opinion focuses on how redistricting battles can create opportunities for politicians to strengthen their electoral positions. The column directs its message to Black voters in Florida.
